title: 10ftv8x
Saqifa of Banu Sa'ida and the process of bay'a
hook: While the Prophet's body was still being washed, the bay'a was taken at Saqifa. The Ahl al-Bayt were left alone at the funeral.
scenes.0.text: The Prophet died in his home in Medina. There was a deep mourning in the house. **Ali**, the Prophet's uncle **Abbas**, and Hashim's sons were at the funeral. It was up to them to wash and bury the Prophet's body. The water's heated in the yard, the shroud's ready. Ali rubbed his arms to wash the Prophet with his own hands and did not leave his head for a moment. Outside the gate, the city was in a different kind of turmoil. A meeting was being arranged to discuss who would take over after the Prophet. While the family was busy with the funeral in tears, someone was walking away at the same time.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: qhlvls
Banu Hashim
scenes.1.text: At the same time, the Ansar, the indigenous Muslims of Medina, gathered in the shade of the sons of Bani Said. This covered courtyard was called Sakife. The head of the Hazrec tribe, **Sa'd b. Ubade**, was ill, but he was there. The Ansar wanted the kingdom to be given to one of their own after the Prophet. It was hot under the shadows, and the voices were getting louder. The Prophet's body had not yet been washed. At this meeting, the announcement made by the Prophet in Ghadir Hum a few months ago by raising the hand of **Ali** was never discussed. The only thing that was discussed was which tribe would take over.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 13r2a44
The Ansar
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: arlxb3
Sa'd b. Ubada
scenes.2.text: When Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayd heard about the meeting, they quickly went to Sakife. They attended the meeting directly, without informing **Ali**, who was at the funeral. Abu Bakr began by praising the Ansar. He told of their help and sacrifice to Islam. He then said that he would not leave the rule of the Arabs to any tribe except the Quraysh. This turned the dispute into a race between the Ansar and Quraysh. The closest to the Prophet in Quraysh was his uncle's son and son-in-law, Ali. He's the one who raised his hand at Ghadir. But at that time, Ali was washing the Prophet's body and no one mentioned his name in Sakife.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 13r2a44
The Ansar
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.2.art.actors.2.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.2.art.actors.3.label: 1suddrx
Abu Ubayda
scenes.3.text: Under the cover of darkness, the argument heated up. **Hubab b. Munzir** of the Ansar stood up and proposed a solution: "Let there be an order from us, an order from you". But Bashir b. Sa'd of the Ensar spoke in favour of Quraysh. That was a crack in the Ensar's own ranks. The old rivalry between the two great tribes of Medina, the Evs and the Hazrec, has resurfaced. The House didn't want Sa'd of Hazrec to take over. Years of resentments moved into the shadows in a matter of hours. So who would be the caliph was not determined by the word of the Prophet, but by counting among the tribes.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 18o1s5l
Hubab b. Mundhir
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1adi38t
Bashir b. Sa'd
scenes.4.text: At the most tense moment of the argument, Umar took Abu Bakr's hand and gave him a bead. Immediately afterwards, the Five and some of the Housemates reached out. It was so tense that someone shouted, "You killed Sa'd!" Sa'd b. But Ubade refused and stayed in the shade, sick. In a matter of hours, the leader of the Muslims was appointed. At that time, **Ali** was still at the Prophet's house, washing his body. And the sons of Hashem were there. Not a single member of the Prophet's family was present when the decision was made.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.5.text: Years later, during his own caliphate, Umar recited a long sermon in Medina. In this sermon, he said about the biat on Sakife's day: "The biat to Ebu Bekir was a felte. Allah has protected him from the evil of it". Felte means a decision made hastily and without consultation. Umar added that something like this should never happen again. That's the word in Buhari. So the decision in Sakife was made in haste, as someone who lived that day would admit. The Shi'ites draw attention to this confession. A decision taken without consultation left out the person who should have been consulted most, the Prophet Ali, who had raised his hand in the Ghadir.
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.6.text: He refused to accept the pledge made in **Ali** Sakife. For six months, he stood beside his wife, **Fatima**. These were Fatima's most difficult days since her father. Fadak was taken from him, threatened to burn the house to the ground. When Fatima passed away, Ali's loneliness grew even greater. Yet he did not draw his sword. The Prophet was patient so that his nation would not be divided and his brother's blood would not be shed. This silence did not mean that he had renounced his right. He didn't forget the proclamation at Ghadir, but he put the unity of the nation ahead of his own. The Shiites remember this patience as one of the greatest sacrifices of Ali.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.7.text: After Fatima's death, people's attitude towards **Ali** changed. The respect that was shown to Fatima while she was alive has disappeared with her passing. Buhari 4240, describes how Ali found people's faces strange during this period. This coldness in the streets of Medina is described more clearly in other narratives. Ali used to greet you on the street. People wouldn't greet you. The Prophet's closest relative, Fatimah's wife and the father of Hasan and Husayn, was a man who was unwelcome in his own city.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.8.text: At night, when Medina was buried in silence, **Ali** would leave his house and go to a well alone. No one would be around. He would stand at the well, put his hands on the edge of the well. Then he'd pour it into the well. He would talk about the pain of losing his wife, **Fatima**, and the rejection of his rights. He never complained day or night, and he never cried out in fear of bloodshed. But at night he would lighten the burden on his heart at the bottom of this well. The stars were shining in the sky, and the palm trees were gently shaken by the wind. In the morning, he would return to the city with a calm face, showing no one his luggage again.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.text: Years passed, and Umar became c**aliph** after Abu Bakr. When Umar was wounded in an assassination attempt, he formed a council of six to elect his successor as caliph. That was the advisory board that met to make the decision. Ali was one of those six. At the end of the council, **Abdurrahman b. Avf** offered the caliphate to Ali on one condition: he would follow the path of Abu Bakr and Umar along with the Quran and the Sunnah. Ali said he would act on his own initiative, along with the Quran and the Sunnah. Uthman accepted the same condition and became the caliph. Ali recalled these days in his Shikshakyaya address, which he read years later, saying that he was patient when he had a thorn in his eye and a bone in his throat.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: 18i2n4z
Abd al-Rahman b. Awf
scenes.9.art.actors.2.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar's long sermon: that the bay'a of Caliph Abu Bakr was a "falta," that God averted its evil, that it must not be repeated; the debate and tension at Saqifa.
sunni.1.says: Lady Fatima asks Caliph Abu Bakr for her inheritance; she is refused, Lady Fatima becomes estranged and passes away six months later; Imam Ali buries her at night. That while Lady Fatima was alive people held Imam Ali in esteem, and after her passing Imam Ali found the faces of the people unfamiliar, is also in this hadith. It then records that Imam Ali pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr. This card is not evidence for the ruling that he did not pledge allegiance. The phrase "six months" is presented as a sentence attributed to al-Zuhri.
sunni.1.grade: Sahih; the phrase "six months" is debated in the commentaries
sunni.2.says: The same event: Lady Fatima's demand for inheritance, Caliph Abu Bakr's reply and Imam Ali's bay'a.
sunni.3.says: The Saqifa debate, Abu Bakr's sermon, Hubab b. Mundhir and Bashir b. Sa'd. The Banu Hashim's holding back and Sa'd's not pledging allegiance are also mentioned. It contains reports from disputed narrators such as Abu Mikhnaf.
sunni.4.says: That Sa'd b. Ubada did not pledge allegiance and later died in the region of Syria. Al-Waqidi's reports are considered weak.
sunni.5.says: The account of the death and of Saqifa; Abu Bakr's saying "I am not the best of you," with a difference in wording.
sunni.6.says: Reports with differing wording about the Banu Hashim's holding back and the process of bay'a. The chains of transmission are mixed.
sunni.7.says: The shura: six men, Abd al-Rahman b. Awf's condition (the Book, the Sunna and the sira of Caliph Abu Bakr and Caliph Umar), Imam Ali's answer "my own ijtihad," and Caliph Uthman's acceptance. It has variants.
sunni.8.says: After Caliph Umar was wounded, he appointed the shura. The detail of the sira condition may not appear in full here.
sunni.9.says: It is the commentary of a Mu'tazili scholar; it is said to contain reports that the sermon exists in early sources.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali describes the caliphate as having been "put on" by Caliph Abu Bakr, himself being at the center like the pivot of the millstone, his being patient with a thorn in his eye and a bone in his throat, and Caliph Umar's leaving the matter to the shura and counting him as one of them.
shia.0.grade: The compilation has no chain of transmission; Sunni critics question its attribution, Shia scholars maintain that it is also found in sources earlier than al-Radi
shia.1.says: Reports on the evidence of the nass of imamate and of the bequest.
shia.2.says: Imam Ali's bay'a and the events after Saqifa, with an imamate interpretation.
shia.3.says: The events after Saqifa and the account of Lady Fatima's house. The attribution of the present copy of the book to Sulaym is disputed; it is not considered evidence on its own.
shia.4.says: The account of the bequest and the imamate. Its attribution to al-Mas'udi is not certain; it is not considered evidence on its own.
shia.5.says: The account of Saqifa, Imam Ali's holding back and the shura. Al-Ya'qubi's school is disputed; Sunni researchers also use him.
disputes.0.title: 19bzxna
What kind of gathering was Saqifa?
disputes.0.sunni: The Ansar gathered at Saqifa, Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayda came, and the bay'a was taken; the Banu Hashim were not there. In the Sunni reading, this is a consultation held for the good of the Ummah.
disputes.0.shia: The Ansar gathered at Saqifa and the bay'a was taken; there is agreement that the Banu Hashim were not there. In the Shia reading, with the nass at Ghadir standing, this gathering held during the funeral preparations is seen as hasty.
disputes.1.title: ytljen
Caliph Umar's word "falta"
disputes.1.sunni: Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta": a sudden matter without consultation. In the Sunni reading, God averted its evil and Caliph Abu Bakr proved worthy.
disputes.1.shia: Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta": a sudden matter without consultation. In the Shia reading, this word is haste's own expression in his own tongue; the text is common ground.
disputes.2.title: qopm2g
Imam Ali's delay in the bay'a
disputes.2.sunni: Bukhari ties Imam Ali's bay'a to after Lady Fatima's passing; the report speaks of six months. In the Sunni reading, this is the tension of mourning and Fadak, after which the voluntary bay'a came; there are also reports transmitting an earlier bay'a.
disputes.2.shia: Bukhari ties Imam Ali's bay'a to after Lady Fatima's passing; the report speaks of six months. In the Shia reading, this waiting shows that he stayed in Lady Fatima's grief and understood his place in the caliphate through Ghadir.
disputes.3.title: tixtmt
Lady Fatima's house
disputes.3.sunni: Reports of pressure on those gathered around the house are mentioned in Sunni books. In this reading, the graver details are considered weak or are not accepted.
disputes.3.shia: Reports of pressure on those gathered around the house are mentioned in the sources. Shia books relate graver details; the matter is disputed and varies according to the texts.
disputes.4.title: cnrdgc
The Shiqshiqiyya and the shura
disputes.4.sunni: Caliph Umar left the matter to a council of six; the bay'a was given to Caliph Uthman. In the Sunni reading, Imam Ali's answer is his holding to his own ijtihad; some researchers attribute the sermon to al-Sharif al-Radi.
disputes.4.shia: The shura was formed and the bay'a was given to Caliph Uthman; this is narrated in these sources. In the Shia reading, the Shiqshiqiyya belongs to Imam Ali: he recalls with patience that he did not regard the way of the two caliphs as a condition and that he was counted as one of them in the shura.
questions.0: Ali and the sons of Hashim took a bead in Sakife while they were washing the Prophet. Why do you think Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayd went directly to the meeting without informing Ali at the funeral?
questions.1: Ali refused the bequest at Sakife and stayed with Fatima for six months. Why do you think Ali didn't draw his sword for six months?
questions.2: Abu Bakr said he would not leave the rule of the Arabs to any tribe other than the Quraysh. Why do you think Ali, the closest to the Prophet in the Quraysh, was not mentioned for this reason?
questions.3: Caliph Umar said in his speech, "The bead made to Abu Bekir was a curse" and added that it should not be repeated. Why do you think Caliph Umar issued this warning?
summary: The Prophet's family took a pledge in Sakife while preparing for his funeral. It is told in Buhari, where Caliph Umar calls this biata "felte". It is also reported in Sunni sources that Ali's beatification was postponed after Fatimah's death (Buhari, Sahih, no. 4240-4241). In Shia reading, the suffering of the Ehl-i Beyt and the place of 'Ali are commemorated together.
key: The bay'a taken while the funeral was being prepared
notes.0: When the Prophet passed away, the Ansar gathered at Saqifa.
notes.1: Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayda went there too.
notes.2: Bay'a was given to Caliph Abu Bakr; Caliph Umar later described it as a «falta» (Bukhari).
notes.3: Imam Ali and the Banu Hashim were preparing the Prophet's washing and burial.
notes.4: Ali did not give up. He kept quiet to avoid bloodshed. Buhari 4240, describes how people's attitudes changed after Fatima's death; the same hadith also writes Ali's next biat.
notes.5: Ali used to greet people on the street, but people didn't. This sentence is not in Buhari 4240.
notes.6: At night, Ali would go to the well alone and tell of his sorrow and loneliness.
